channel.title: Georgia Public Broadcasting - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Georgia Public Broadcasting (gpb.org)

item.title: How Georgia law complicates the case against Colin Gray
item.description: Prosecutors are using child endangerment laws as the 'predicate offense' for the second-degree murder charges against Colin Gray, says analyst and former U.S. Attorney Michael Moore.

item.title: Georgia Today: Legal fight over seized voter data; School shooting father trial opens; Spike Lee
item.description: On the Feb. 16 edition: A legal fight is brewing over the voter data seized by the FBI; Opening arguments begin in the trial of the father whose son killed four people at Apalachee High School; And Spike Lee talks 'School Daze' and its legacy

item.title: GPB evening headlines for February 16, 2026
item.description: The trial has started for a man whose teenage son is accused in the fatal shooting at Georgia's Apalachee High School. Nineteen candidates vying to replace former U.S. Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene appeared in Atlanta Press Club debates. The NAACP and allied groups are asking a judge to limit how the federal government uses data seized in an FBI raid.

item.title: Music can be medicine. This study examines what a dose of symphony does for dementia
item.description: Earlier research from Emory University’s Goizueta Brain Health Institute found that music improves mood and engagement among people with cognitive concerns. Now, a partnership with the Atlanta Symphony Orchestra is studying how best to use music to improve their lives.

item.title: Frederick Wiseman, who captured the weirdness and wonder of everyday life, dies at 96
item.description: The prolific, pioneering filmmaker made dozens of documentaries and chronicled the inner workings of institutions. His 1967 film, Titicut Follies, revealed appalling conditions at a prison facility.

item.title: The U.S. women's hockey team is dominating the Olympics. Now they will play for gold
item.description: The Americans, whose captain Hilary Knight is leading a generation of thrilling young talent, are undefeated through six games at the Olympics — and they're outscoring their opponents 31 to 1.

item.title: Actor Robert Duvall has died — he brought a compassionate center to edgy hard roles
item.description: Duvall appeared in over 90 films over the course of his career, imbuing stock Hollywood types — cowboys, cops, soldiers — with a nuanced sense of vulnerability.

item.title: A curling scandal rocks Olympic ice
item.description: Allegations of cheating and swearing on the curling ice have rocked the sport after the Swedes accused the Canadians of "double touching" in a match. What happened then, and what's happened since?

item.title: Gold for Elana Meyers Taylor at last! Georgian, 41, wins Olympic monobob title
item.description: Elana Meyers Taylor of the U.S. finally won bobsled gold in her fifth Olympics.

item.title: Two U.S. moms in their 40s rocketed to gold and bronze in Olympic bobsled showdown
item.description: American sliders Elana Meyers Taylor, 41, and Kaillie Humphreys, 40, secure gold and bronze medals. Meyers-Taylor built on her record as the Black athlete with the most Winter Olympics medals.
